intro: Japanese treats a wish as a state that sits in the speaker, not as an action aimed at a thing. That is why the wanted thing can be marked like the subject of an adjective, with が: 水が欲しい is literally "water is wanted (by me)". ～たい keeps one foot in the verb, so its object may keep を; 欲しい is a pure adjective, so its object is が. When you want someone else to act, that person is the one you look to for the action, and takes に: 母に来てほしい.

skills.rule: With ～たい the object takes を or が (を always works); with 欲しい the wanted thing takes が, never を.
skills.explain:
～たい turns a verb into an adjective meaning "want to". Its direct object may stay を or switch to が: 水を飲みたい and 水が飲みたい are both correct. が puts the wish on the thing and sounds a little more immediate; を is neutral and safe everywhere. Prefer を when the object is far from たい, when the verb is long (日本語を勉強したい), or with する-verbs.

Only を can become が. Every other particle stays exactly as the verb needs it: 友達に会いたい, 京都に行きたい, 公園で遊びたい. Never 友達が会いたい or 京都が行きたい.

欲しい ("want" a thing) is an adjective, so its object is が: 新しい靴が欲しい. In negatives and contrasts は replaces が or を: 車は欲しくない, 肉は食べたくない.

Both words state your own wish. For another person use 欲しがる / ～たがる, which take を (妹が猫を欲しがっている), or add そうだ / と言っている.
patterns: [person] に / [place] に・で … [verb stem]たい  (other particles unchanged)
[thing] は 欲しくない / [verb stem]たくない  (negative, contrast)
[third person] が [thing] を 欲しがっている

examples.jp: 冷[つめ]たい水[みず]{が}飲[の]みたいです。
examples.en: I want to drink some cold water.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しいかばん{が}欲[ほ]しいです。
週末[しゅうまつ]は映画[えいが]{を}見[み]たいな。
examples.en: I'd like to watch a film this weekend.

examples.jp: 来年[らいねん]、大学[だいがく]で経済[けいざい]{を}勉強[べんきょう]したいです。
examples.en: Next year I want to study economics at university.

examples.jp: 誕生日[たんじょうび]に何[なに]{が}欲[ほ]しいですか。
examples.en: What do you want for your birthday?

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]は新[あたら]しいゲーム{を}欲[ほ]しがっています。
examples.en: My little brother wants a new game.

contrast.note: に never marks the thing you want. It appears only when the verb itself needs に: 先生に会いたい (meet the teacher), 海に行きたい. If the verb normally takes を, use を or が.
は is not the default for the wanted thing; it adds contrast or comes with a negative: コーヒーは飲みたくない (coffee, at least, I don't want). In a plain positive wish use が or を.
の links two nouns (日本の車). At the end of a sentence it cannot mark the wanted thing: 車の欲しいです is wrong. Only inside a clause that describes a noun may の replace が: 車の欲しい人 (people who want a car).

mistakes.bad: 新[あたら]しいパソコン{を}欲[ほ]しいです。
mistakes.good: 新[あたら]しいパソコン{が}欲[ほ]しいです。
mistakes.note: 欲しい is an adjective: its object is が. を appears only with 欲しがる (someone else's wish).

mistakes.bad: 来月[らいげつ]、北海道[ほっかいどう]{が}行[い]きたいです。
mistakes.good: 来月[らいげつ]、北海道[ほっかいどう]{に}行[い]きたいです。
mistakes.note: Only を may change to が. A destination keeps に (or へ) even before たい.

mistakes.bad: 田中[たなか]さんは車[くるま]{が}欲[ほ]しいです。
mistakes.good: 田中[たなか]さんは車[くるま]{を}欲[ほ]しがっています。
mistakes.note: 欲しい and ～たい state your own feelings. For a third person use 欲しがる / ～たがる with を.

skills.tip: Ask: would the plain verb take を? Then を or が. Anything else stays put. 欲しい: always が.

skills.rule: To want someone to do something, mark that person with に: [person] に [verb て-form] ほしい.
skills.explain:
～てほしい means "I want someone to do". The doer is the person you want the action from, so they take に: 父にたばこをやめてほしい (I want my father to quit smoking). The action keeps its own particles: たばこを stays を. The same に appears with ～てもらいたい, a slightly politer variant: 先生にもう一度説明してもらいたい.

The negative is ～ないでほしい: 弟に私の部屋に入らないでほしい (I don't want my brother coming into my room).

When the thing you want to happen has no human doer, mark it with が: 早く春が来てほしい, 雨がやんでほしい. With people, に is the standard choice. When the doer is obvious, especially "you", simply drop it: 静かにしてほしい.

Do not use ～たい here: 母に来たい does not mean "I want my mother to come". ～たい is always about the speaker's own action.
patterns: [person] に [object を] [verb て-form] ほしい
[person] に [verb ない-form] ないでほしい
[person] に [verb て-form] もらいたい
[event, no human doer] が [verb て-form] ほしい

examples.jp: 母[はは]{に}早[はや]く帰[かえ]ってきてほしいです。
examples.en: I want my mother to come home early.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さん{に}この仕事[しごと]を手伝[てつだ]ってほしい。
examples.en: I want Mr Tanaka to help with this job.

examples.jp: 子供[こども]たち{に}もっと本[ほん]を読[よ]んでほしいです。
examples.en: I want the children to read more books.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]{に}このことは誰[だれ]にも言[い]わないでほしい。
examples.en: I don't want my friend to tell anyone about this.

examples.jp: 医者[いしゃ]{に}もう一度[いちど]説明[せつめい]してもらいたいです。
examples.en: I'd like the doctor to explain it once more.

contrast.note: を marks what the person does, not the person: 兄に車を貸してほしい (I want my brother to lend me the car). The person themselves is never を.
が is right for things that happen by themselves: 雨がやんでほしい, バスが早く来てほしい. For a person whose action you are hoping for, use に.
と means "with" or "together with": 父と旅行したい is a trip you take with your father. 父に旅行してほしい is a trip you want him to take.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]{を}ゆっくり話[はな]してほしいです。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]{に}ゆっくり話[はな]してほしいです。
mistakes.note: The person who is to act takes に, not を.

mistakes.bad: 妹[いもうと]{に}来[き]たいです。
mistakes.good: 妹[いもうと]{に}来[き]てほしいです。
mistakes.note: ～たい is only for your own action. To want someone else to act, use the て-form plus ほしい.

mistakes.bad: 部長[ぶちょう]{で}この書類[しょるい]を見[み]てほしいです。
mistakes.good: 部長[ぶちょう]{に}この書類[しょるい]を見[み]てほしいです。
mistakes.note: で marks a place or means, never the person you want something from.

skills.tip: Who should do it? Put に after them, then て-form + ほしい. No human doer (rain, spring, the bus)? が.
